subject: Banking
title: How to Read Your Credit Report
description: A fast breakdown of How to Read Your Credit Report for builders.

hook.text: Your credit report is a financial biography. It lists every loan, card.

buildup.text: The report has four sections: personal info, account history, inquiries, and public records like bankruptcies or liens.

discovery.text: Account history shows each account's credit limit, balance, payment status, and whether it's current or delinquent.

twist.text: Negative items stay for 7 years. Bankruptcies stay for 10. But their impact on your score fades each year.

climax.text: Your credit report is public knowledge to lenders. Understanding what's in it is the first step to controlling it.

punchline.text: Seven years of history. Lenders see everything. You should see it first.

quiz.question: How long do negative items typically stay on a credit report?
